title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
abstract: arXiv:2611.27891v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. Building on this observation, we introduce DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection), which pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification. By combining these known draws with predictions from an existing drafter, DICE allocates computation toward continuations more likely to be used in the current sampling run. translated_title: 投机解码没有你想象的那么“投机”
translated_abstract: 投机解码通过在目标模型生成之前预先准备好候选续写内容来加速语言模型推理。其效率取决于有限的草稿计算能在多大程度上预测目标模型实际将走的路径。预测这条路径涉及两个不确定性来源：目标模型的预测以及采样的随机性。然而，前者需要目标模型的前向传播计算，而后者可以在草稿生成之前就被确定下来。基于这一观察，我们提出了DICE（基于抽取信息的候选选择，Draw-Informed Candidate Selection），它预先采样并在草稿生成与验证之间同步验证随机性。通过将这些已知的抽取结果与现有草稿模型的预测相结合，DICE将计算资源分配给更可能在当前采样运行中被使用的续写内容。这一原则贯穿草稿树构建过程中的节点选择，并扩展到异步预取场景中。
tldr: 本文提出DICE方法，通过预先采样并在草稿生成与验证阶段之间同步采样随机性，将有限的草稿计算集中于更可能被目标模型实际采用的候选续写，从而提升投机解码的推理效率。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DICE, a method that pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification, allocating limited draft computation toward candidate continuations more likely to be accepted, thereby improving the efficiency of speculative decoding.
